'''Maharaj Kishan Bhan''' (9 November 1947 – 26 January 2020) was an Indian [[pediatrics|pediatrician]] and clinical scientist.<ref>{{cite news|title=Maharaj Kishan Bhan Aims For a New Bio Culture |url=http://forbesindia.com/article/big-bet/maharaj-kishan-bhan-aims-for-a-new-bio-culture/24532/1|access-date=17 August 2012|newspaper=Forbes|date=4 May 2011}}</ref>  He received [[M.B.B.S.]] Degree (1969) from [[Armed Forces Medical College, Pune]] and [[M.D.]] Degree from [[Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research]], [[Chandigarh]]. He carried out extensive post doctoral research at [[All India Institute of Medical Sciences]] in the areas of diarrheal diseases and child nutrition with an emphasis on [[public health]] issues. He served as the president of the [[JIPMER|Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research (JIPMER)]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://jipmer.edu.in/dr-mk-bhan-president-jipmer/|title=President, JIPMER|access-date=13 June 2016|archive-date=7 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181207155137/http://jipmer.edu.in/dr-mk-bhan-president-jipmer/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was known for developing Rota Viral Vaccine in collaboration with [[Bharat Biotech]] International. He was positioned as Secretary, [[Department of Biotechnology]], [[Government of India]], until 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shaping Technologies into Real Life Programs|url=http://biospectrumindia.ciol.com/cgi-bin/printer.asp?id=78001|access-date=17 August 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209190605/http://biospectrumindia.ciol.com/cgi-bin/printer.asp?id=78001|archive-date=9 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bhan conceived the newly formed BIRAC, which is expected to result in product development by industry in collaboration with academia. This initiative is to boost product development in the country. For this Bhan was actively assisted by Renu Swarup and Ravi Dhar from BIRAC. An elected fellow of the [[National Academy of Medical Sciences]],<ref name="List of FellowsNAMS">{{cite web | url=http://www.nams-india.in/downloads/fellowsmembers/ZZ.pdf | title=List of Fellows&nbsp;— NAMS | publisher=National Academy of Medical Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=19 March 2016}}</ref> he was awarded in 1990 the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], the highest science award in [[India]], in the Medical Sciences category.<ref>{{cite web|title=Full list of winners of the Shanti Swaroop Prize|url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/13729624/Bhatnagar-Prize-Winner#page=70|access-date=17 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111028213140/http://www.scribd.com/doc/13729624/Bhatnagar-Prize-Winner#page=70|archive-date=28 October 2011}}</ref>  He held honorary [[Doctor of Science]] and was responsible for policy formulation and was Member of the Jury for nearly all major national science awards awarded by the [[Government of India]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Speakers Bios|url=http://www.stanford.edu/group/biodesign/cgi-bin/indianmedtechsummit/?page_id=17|work=Indian Medtech Summit|access-date=17 August 2012|archive-date=10 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101210174350/http://www.stanford.edu/group/biodesign/cgi-bin/indianmedtechsummit/?page_id=17|url-status=dead}}</ref>
